ex.en: The dog loves its new toy.
I bought a toy for my nephew's birthday.
Could you put the toys away?
Want to go to an art exhibition this weekend?
That exhibition runs until next week.
I'm busy at work preparing for an exhibition.

note: 틈(이) 나다 = to have a free moment.

ex.en: Wind is coming in through the gap in the window.
Call me when you get a free moment.
I'm so busy lately I have no time to rest.
Let me say just one thing before the meeting ends.

ex.s: 그 사람은 저녁 내내 한마디도 안 했어요.
ex.en: He didn't say a single word all evening.
It was my birthday, and not even a word of congratulations.

note: Konglish: also a group blind date among students.

ex.en: I have a meeting at 3 p.m.
The meeting ran long, so I'm a bit late.
I often went on group blind dates in college.
I called the boss's secretary.

ex.s: 제 비서가 일정을 보내 드릴 거예요.
ex.en: My assistant will send you the schedule.

ex.s: 휴대폰 음성 비서한테 알람을 맞춰 달라고 했어요.
ex.en: I asked my phone's voice assistant to set an alarm.
I put candles on the birthday cake.
This café's cheesecake is delicious.

ex.s: 케이크 한 조각 더 먹어도 돼요?
ex.en: Can I have another slice of cake?

en: to get (something) on; to be buried
note: Causative/passive of 묻다. 손에 물 묻히다 = get your hands wet.

ex.en: The kid got ice cream on their clothes.

ex.s: 상처 났으니까 손에 물 묻히지 마세요.
ex.en: You have a cut, so don't get your hands wet.
My grandfather is buried in his hometown.

note: Often 적혀 있다 = to be written on something.

ex.en: The prices aren't written on the menu.
Call the number written here.
The homework was written on the board.

en: this way, this side; this person
note: 이쪽은 제 남편이에요 = This is my husband (introducing).

ex.en: The restroom is at the end on this side.
Right this way, please.
This is my friend Ji-woo.

note: Used with 춤: 춤을 추다. 추어요 → 춰요.

ex.en: We danced together at the wedding.
I'm not good at dancing.
The kid is dancing to the song.

note: 정(이) 들다 = to grow attached. 정이 많다 = warm-hearted.

ex.en: I've grown really attached to this neighborhood.
The ladies at the market are really warm-hearted.
I got attached to the puppy, so it's hard to give it away.

note: 소원을 빌다 = to make a wish.

ex.en: Did you make a wish in front of the birthday cake?
My wish is to travel the world.
Just grant me one wish.

note: Address as 강사님.

ex.en: The yoga instructor is really kind.
I work as an English instructor at a private academy.
The instructor is sick, so today's class was canceled.

note: 쇼핑하다 = to shop.

ex.en: I'm going shopping with a friend this weekend.
These days I shop online a lot.

ex.s: 여행 가서 쇼핑을 너무 많이 했어요.
ex.en: I did way too much shopping on the trip.

note: Two different verbs: 머리를 말리다 (dry), 싸움을 말리다 (stop).

ex.en: I'll dry my hair and head right out.
The weather's nice, so I'm drying the laundry outside.
My friends were fighting, so I stopped them.

note: Konglish: means a dress, not a swimsuit.

ex.en: Can I try on this dress?
Which dress are you wearing to the wedding?
It was hot, so I wore a dress.
Yesterday I signed up at a gym near home.
I need to register for next semester's classes.
I registered my new card in the app.

note: 티(가) 나다 = to show. 티 내다 = to let it show.

ex.en: It shows on your face that you're tired.

ex.s: 면접관 앞에서 긴장한 티 내지 마세요.
ex.en: Don't let the interviewers see you're nervous.
I wore a white T-shirt and jeans.

note: Casual slang; 진상 부리다 = act like a jerk. Formal homonym: the truth.

ex.en: A nightmare customer came into the shop today.
Don't act like a jerk after drinking.
In the end, the truth about it came out.
Please sign here.

ex.s: 계약서에 서명하기 전에 꼭 읽어 보세요.
ex.en: Be sure to read the contract before you sign it.
I signed when I received the package.

note: 호랑이도 제 말 하면 온다 = speak of the devil.

ex.en: I saw a tiger at the zoo for the first time.
Our teacher is as scary as a tiger.

ex.s: 호랑이도 제 말 하면 온다더니, 민호가 왔네요!
ex.en: Speak of the devil, here comes Minho!
Kids love adventure stories.
Traveling alone was a big adventure.

ex.s: 지금 회사를 옮기는 건 좀 모험이에요.
ex.en: Changing jobs now is a bit of a gamble.

note: 안내하다 = to guide. 안내 데스크 = information desk.

ex.en: Where's the information desk?
Listen carefully to the subway announcements.

ex.s: 회사 첫날에 선배가 안내를 해 줬어요.
ex.en: On my first day at work, a senior coworker showed me around.
Our friendship will last forever.

ex.s: 이 반지는 친구랑 산 우정 반지예요.
ex.en: This is a friendship ring I bought with my friend.
The friendship fell apart over money.

note: Marks a small consolation: things aren't great, but…

ex.s: 비가 오지만 그나마 바람은 안 불어요.
ex.en: It's raining, but at least it's not windy.
At least you weren't badly hurt, thank goodness.

ex.s: 월급이 적은데 그나마 다 써 버렸어요.
ex.en: My paycheck is small, and I spent even that.

note: Casual spoken form of 그렇지만.

ex.en: It's tasty. But it's a bit pricey.

ex.s: 가고 싶어요. 그치만 내일 출근해야 해요.
ex.en: I want to go. But I have to work tomorrow.
I know. But I'm too tired today.

note: Casual form of 만날; often used when complaining.

ex.en: You can't eat just ramyeon all the time.
My little brother always gets up late.
Why do you always do this only to me?
I ran into my teacher at the supermarket.

ex.s: 길을 잃었는데 우연히 좋은 식당을 찾았어요.
ex.en: I got lost and found a great restaurant by chance.

ex.s: 여행 중에 우연히 옛날 친구를 봤어요.
ex.en: I happened to see an old friend while traveling.
I put the winter clothes in storage.
Could you bring a box from the storage room?
Those shoes are out of stock in the warehouse too.

note: Bow + 안녕하세요 is the standard greeting.

ex.en: Say hello to Grandma first.
I said hi to my neighbor in the elevator.
I went to say hello to the new team members.

note: ㅂ-irregular: 차가워요. Cold weather is 춥다.

ex.en: The pool water is too cold.
Why are your hands so cold?

ex.s: 그 사람은 처음엔 좀 차가워 보였어요.
ex.en: He seemed a bit cold at first.

en: to stretch out, reach; to crash (exhausted)

ex.en: Stretch out your legs and sit comfortably.
I reached out and grabbed the cup.
I was so tired I crashed as soon as I got home.
Please take off your shoes indoors.
It's raining, so let's play inside.

ex.s: 실내 수영장이 있는 호텔을 찾고 있어요.
ex.en: I'm looking for a hotel with an indoor pool.
I boiled potatoes for dinner.
A burger and an order of fries, please.
I bought a bag of potatoes at the market.
The kid says they dreamed about a monster.

ex.s: 이 영화에 나오는 괴물이 너무 무서워요.
ex.en: The monster in this movie is so scary.
That athlete is an absolute beast.

note: 드라이브하다 / 드라이브 가다 = go for a drive. Not for commuting.

ex.en: Want to go for a drive to the beach this weekend?
I like going for drives at night.
I went for a drive to clear my head.
It's fall, so the leaves have all fallen.
The leaves on the potted plant turned yellow.
You wrap the meat in a lettuce leaf and eat it.
Someone stole my wallet on the subway.

ex.s: 강아지가 또 제 양말을 훔쳐 갔어요.
ex.en: The dog stole my sock again.
You shouldn't steal other people's ideas.
I put the keys on the table.
Put your bags on the overhead shelf.
I left my phone on the checkout counter.
I donated clothes I don't wear.
I donate a little every month.
Our company donated computers to a school.
I set my phone alarm for six.

ex.s: 은행 앱 비밀번호를 새로 설정해야 해요.
ex.en: I need to set a new password for the bank app.
Don't set your goals too high.
The doctor warned me to quit smoking.
Mom warned me not to be late.

ex.s: 미리 경고하는데, 이 집 엄청 매워요.
ex.en: I'm warning you now, this place is super spicy.
Want me to peel a tangerine for you?
Help me peel the garlic.
Everyone online is trashing that movie.
I spilled coffee on my keyboard.
I bought a new keyboard and it sounds nice.
My younger sibling plays keyboard in a band.

note: 불행하게도 = unfortunately.

ex.en: I was really unhappy back then.
You can be unhappy even with lots of money.
Unfortunately, the flight was canceled.

note: Casual slang, fine with friends. Also 'super' before adjectives: 짱 좋다.

ex.en: This tteokbokki is seriously awesome!
My mom's cooking is the best.
The weather is super nice today.
Are you suspecting me right now?
At first I doubted that story.
The doctor suspected a stomach bug.

note: 긴장하다 / 긴장되다 = to be nervous. 긴장(을) 풀다 = relax.

ex.en: I'm so nervous about tomorrow's interview.
Relax and take it easy.
I still get nervous when I drive.

note: ㅂ-irregular: 두려워요. Less everyday than 무섭다; often fear of situations.

ex.s: 혼자 외국에 가는 게 좀 두려워요.
ex.en: I'm a little afraid of going abroad alone.
I'm afraid I'll make mistakes at my new job.
I was scared of the surgery, so I kept putting it off.

note: Followed by a counter: 수천 명, 수천 개.

ex.en: Thousands of people came to the concert.
This bag costs thousands of dollars.

ex.s: 캠핑장 하늘에 별이 수천 개 있었어요.
ex.en: There were thousands of stars over the campsite.

note: Formal; in daily speech 내다 or 계산하다 is more common.

ex.en: I don't have cash, so I'll pay by card.
I paid for the hotel in advance.
The company pays my transportation costs.
It's really cold outside.
I'll wait outside.
The kids are playing outside.

note: ㅂ-irregular: 날카로워요.

ex.en: The knife is sharp, so be careful.
The cat's claws are sharper than you'd think.
The professor's question was really sharp.

note: More formal; 대답하다 is more common in speech.

ex.en: Please reply to my text quickly.
I answered the interview questions honestly.
They give you a coupon if you answer the survey.
These strawberries are really sweet.

ex.s: 저녁 먹고 달콤한 디저트 먹고 싶어요.
ex.en: I want a sweet dessert after dinner.
Sleeping in on weekends is so sweet.
The little kid next door is so cute.
A little kid was crying at the restaurant.

ex.s: 우리 아들이 꼬마일 때 여기 자주 왔어요.
ex.en: We came here often when our son was little.

note: Excludes the number: 19세 미만 = under 19. 이하 includes it.

ex.en: No one under 19 can go in.
Orders under 50,000 won have a shipping fee.
Kids under 3 get in free.
I blocked that person's number.
Do you know how to block spam texts?
Sunscreen blocks the sun.
Please clean up your room.
I'll clear the table after we finish eating.
I tidied the meeting room and went home.

note: Formal (forms, interviews); everyday is 원하다 or 바라다.

ex.en: What's your desired salary?
Many students hope to go to grad school.
Choose your preferred delivery date.
The lion was sleeping at the zoo.
My kid loves the stuffed lion the most.
I saw lions in person on my trip to Africa.

ex.s: 저는 높은 곳에 대한 두려움이 있어요.
ex.en: I have a fear of heights.

ex.s: 두려움 때문에 아무 말도 못 했어요.
ex.en: I couldn't say anything out of fear.

ex.s: 수영을 배우고 물에 대한 두려움이 없어졌어요.
ex.en: After learning to swim, my fear of water went away.

note: Followed by a counter: 수십 번, 수십 명.

ex.en: I called dozens of times yesterday.

ex.s: 식당 앞에 수십 명이 줄을 서 있었어요.
ex.en: Dozens of people were lined up outside the restaurant.

ex.s: 아버지는 이 일을 수십 년 하셨어요.
ex.en: My father did this work for decades.

note: 녹음하다 = to record. Video recording is 녹화.

ex.en: May I record the class?
I recorded the meeting on my phone.
I'm going to a studio this weekend to record a song.

note: Same as 부족하다.

ex.en: I'm a little short on money this month.
I haven't had enough sleep, so I'm exhausted.

ex.s: 손님이 더 와서 의자가 하나 모자라요.
ex.en: More guests came, so we're one chair short.

note: Pronounced [흑]; 흙이 → [흘기].

ex.en: There's dirt on my shoes.
I added more soil to the pot.
The kids are playing with dirt at the playground.
After three years, I finally did it!

ex.s: 이번 시험도 분명히 해낼 수 있어요.
ex.en: You can definitely pull off this exam too.
I managed the whole move by myself.
The culprit who ate the cake was our dog.
I can't figure out who the culprit is in this drama.
I heard the police caught the culprit.
When I moved, I threw out everything unnecessary.

ex.s: 우리 회사는 불필요한 회의가 너무 많아요.
ex.en: Our company has too many unnecessary meetings.
I deleted unnecessary apps from my phone.

note: Follows a noun: 산 너머 = beyond the mountain.

ex.en: You can see the ocean through the hotel window.

ex.s: 전화기 너머로 아기 우는 소리가 들렸어요.
ex.en: I heard a baby crying on the other end of the phone.

ex.s: 저 산 너머에 작은 마을이 있어요.
ex.en: There's a small village beyond that mountain.
They say he caught the flu virus at the hospital.
Disinfect the wound so it doesn't get infected.
My work computer got a virus.

note: 초점(을) 맞추다 = to focus (on).

ex.en: This photo is out of focus.

ex.s: 너무 피곤해서 눈 초점이 안 맞아요.
ex.en: I'm so tired my eyes won't focus.
This meeting will focus on costs.

note: Supporting role is 조연.

ex.en: Who's the lead in this drama?
That actor got a lead role for the first time.
Our daughter played the lead in the school play.

note: In speech 일본 사람 is more common.

ex.en: My roommate is Japanese.
The owner of that ramen shop is Japanese.
There are lots of Japanese tourists in this area.

en: to deal with; to face (an opponent)

ex.en: Dealing with a nightmare customer wore me out.
It's hard to handle three kids by yourself.
That team is really tough to play against.

note: 애정이 가다 = to feel attached to.

ex.en: Grandma has so much affection for her grandkids.

ex.s: 오래 탄 차라서 애정이 많이 가요.
ex.en: I've driven this car a long time, so I'm attached to it.

ex.s: 일에 애정이 있어야 오래 할 수 있어요.
ex.en: You have to love your work to stick with it.

note: Homonym: suffix -용 means 'for' (선물용 = for a gift).

ex.en: The kid drew a picture of a dragon.
My Chinese zodiac sign is the dragon.
A huge dragon appears in that movie.
That company treats its employees well.
We got VIP treatment at that hotel.

ex.s: 저도 이제 어른 대우를 해 주세요.
ex.en: Please treat me like an adult now.
The kid built a house out of blocks.

ex.s: 밤에 레고 블록을 밟아서 발이 아파요.
ex.en: I stepped on a Lego brick last night and my foot hurts.

ex.s: 두 블록 더 가면 은행이 있어요.
ex.en: Go two more blocks and there's a bank.

note: Used as 충격적이다 or 충격적인 + noun.

ex.en: That news was really shocking.
The movie's ending is so shocking.
Housing prices here are shockingly high.

note: Usually means 'hot topic' or 'matter,' not 'problem.'

ex.en: That actor is a hot topic online these days.
We discussed that issue in today's meeting.
Is anything big going on at school these days?

en: to crack, chap; start speaking casually
note: 말을 트다 = to switch to casual speech (반말).

ex.en: It's winter, so my lips are all chapped.
My hands were chapped, so I put on hand cream.
Should we start talking casually now?

note: 환상적이다 = fantastic. 환상의 콤비 = dream team.

ex.en: I had a fantasy about what marriage would be like.
My illusions about Paris were shattered on the trip.

ex.s: 두 사람은 일할 때 환상의 콤비예요.
ex.en: Those two are a dream team at work.
Have you been to the Busan film festival?
That movie won an award at a film festival.
I entered a short film in the school film festival.
The tteokbokki booth was the most popular at the festival.

ex.s: 박람회에서 회사 부스를 하루 종일 지켰어요.
ex.en: I staffed our company booth at the expo all day.
I took pictures with friends in a photo booth.

note: 문구점 = stationery store.

ex.en: I bought pens and notebooks at the stationery store.

ex.s: 딸은 예쁜 문구를 모으는 걸 좋아해요.
ex.en: My daughter loves collecting cute stationery.
Did you decide what to write on the cake?
I'm trying to improve my eating habits lately.
The company has really improved working conditions.
I practice every day to improve my pronunciation.

note: Card approval at checkout uses the noun: 승인이 안 됐어요.

ex.en: My manager approved my vacation.
The bank approved my loan.
The school approved our club.
The logo on this T-shirt is too big.
Our company changed its logo.

ex.s: 이 카페는 컵에 있는 로고가 귀여워요.
ex.en: The logo on this café's cups is cute.

note: 커버하다 can also mean to cover for someone.

ex.en: I bought a new phone case.
I washed the sofa cover over the weekend.
That singer did a cover of this song.

note: 인간적으로 = on a human level; honestly (casual).

ex.en: My team leader is really warm and decent.
I like that actor's human side.
Honestly, this price is way too high.

note: 면역력 = immune strength, common in health talk.

ex.en: My immunity is down lately, so I get sick often.
Kids build up immunity as they grow.
I've become immune to spicy food now.
After getting sick, I realized the importance of health.
I teach kids the importance of reading.
At work, I really feel how important communication is.

note: Used as 이상적이다 or 이상적인 + noun. 이상형 = ideal type (dating).

ex.en: Today is ideal weather for a picnic.
Ten minutes to work would be ideal.
What's the ideal weight for my height?
Anyone who had contact with the patient, please get tested.

ex.s: 세제가 피부에 접촉하지 않게 장갑을 끼세요.
ex.en: Wear gloves so the detergent doesn't touch your skin.

ex.s: 그 회사 담당자와 먼저 접촉해 볼게요.
ex.en: I'll try reaching out to their contact person first.
Minho is the ace of our soccer team.
Su-jin is the sales star at our company.

ex.s: 우리 반 에이스가 시험에서 또 1등 했어요.
ex.en: Our class's top student came first on the test again.

note: 활약하다 = to play an active role, shine.

ex.s: 어제 경기에서 그 선수 활약이 대단했어요.
ex.en: That player was amazing in yesterday's game.

ex.s: 이번 프로젝트에서 지우 씨 활약이 컸어요.
ex.en: Ji-woo played a big part in this project.

ex.s: 그 배우는 요즘 해외에서 활약하고 있어요.
ex.en: That actor is active overseas these days.

note: Say 장인어른 to him. Husband's father is 시아버지.

ex.en: I'm going to my father-in-law's this weekend.
My father-in-law really loves fishing.
A master craftsman made this bowl by hand.

ex.s: 학원에서 배운 표현을 실전에서 써 봤어요.
ex.en: I tried using phrases from class in real life.
I've practiced driving, but this is my first time for real.

ex.s: 시험 전에 실전 문제를 많이 풀어요.
ex.en: Before the exam, I do lots of real exam-style questions.
